## Simple explanation

Training is how a model learns from examples. The system makes predictions,
measures errors against a learning objective, and adjusts model parameters
to improve performance.

## Technical explanation

Training optimizes model parameters using an objective function and an
optimization algorithm. It can involve supervised labels, self-supervised
targets, rewards, or other signals. Data preparation, batching, numerical
precision, and stopping criteria are part of the training system.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Training decisions shape model capability, generalization, cost, and
reproducibility. A successful training run is not sufficient evidence of
quality; models still require evaluation, deployment testing, and
monitoring.

## How it works

The training loop loads a batch, computes model outputs and loss,
calculates gradients, and updates parameters. It repeats across batches
and epochs, while validation checks guide model selection and checkpointing.

## Practical example

A classifier trains on labeled examples using cross-entropy loss and an
optimizer. The team monitors validation performance and stops or adjusts
training if the model begins to overfit.

## Common misconceptions

- Lower training loss does not guarantee better performance on unseen or
  deployment data.
- Training and inference are different workloads; a model that trains on
  one device may need different optimization to serve efficiently.
